## What is not in R yet {#what-is-not-in-r-yet}

`matisseR` (version 0.1.0) ports the core of MATISSE: rates objects, the New APC model with five estimable functions, and CAPRICORN. It adds the generation and share tools you met in Module 4. Several other MATISSE methods exist **only in the MATLAB toolbox**, which Philip S. Rosenberg wrote and which remains the reference implementation.

| Method | What it does | MATLAB | Read more |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Smoothing Lexis diagrams** | Denoises a matrix of rates with a panel of kernel filters, keeping an optimal balance of bias and variance | `sift`, `panko` | [Smoothing methods for Lexis diagrams](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/09622802231192950) |
| **SAGE** (semiparametric APC) | Smooths the observed rates with SIFT, then fits the New APC model to the smoothed rates. Gives smoother estimable functions, which helps most when counts per cell are modest | `sage` | [Cancer incidence trends in successive social generations, JAMA Netw Open 2024](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2819747) |
| **EPIPHANY** (exploratory comparative APC) | Given K groups, finds the best-fitting partition into proportional subsets and non-proportional singletons, so you can group estimable functions as equal, parallel or unequal | `epiphany` | [Comparative APC analysis, BMC Med Res Methodol 2023](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12874-023-02039-8) |
| **Joinpoint regression** | Piecewise linear trends with the number and location of knots chosen from the data | `joinpoint` | [Joinpoint method paper](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10649300/) |
| **Standard plots and summary curves** | The four standard plots of rates (versus period, age or cohort) and marginal summary curves | `rates` methods `salsa`, `ftp`, `line`, `sierra`, `scan` | [Toolbox guide](../matlab/toolbox.qmd) |
| **More estimable functions** | Gradient shifts, deviations, rate ratios, and likelihood-ratio and Wald tests for APC submodels | `apc` methods `ef`, `lrt`, `wald`, `aic` | [Toolbox guide](../matlab/toolbox.qmd) |

::: {.callout-note title="A note on validation"}
`matisseR` has an internal test suite, and a folder in the package sets up a side-by-side comparison of R and MATLAB results on the same data. The MATLAB side of that comparison has not been run yet, so treat the two as equivalent in method but not yet cross-checked number by number.
:::

The MATISSE system map shows where every class and method sits. The R package covers part of it.

![](../images/system_map.png){fig-alt="Subway-style map of MATISSE classes and methods: rates, apc, epiphany, capricorn, sift, sage, panko, joinpoint and matrix." width="70%"}

## Choose a tool {#choose-a-tool}

| You want to... | Use |
|---|---|
| Fit the New APC model, read the estimable functions, compare groups with CAPRICORN | **R** (`matisseR`) or MATLAB; the methods are the same |
| Compare social generations, cohort shares, or pool results across many populations in a script | **R**: these tools are in `matisseR` only |
| Run many analyses reproducibly in a pipeline | **R** |
| Smooth sparse rates, fit SAGE, run EPIPHANY, fit joinpoint models, draw the four standard plots | **MATLAB** until they are ported |

You do not have to choose once. A common workflow smooths and fits in MATLAB, then moves rate tables to R for the generation and pooling steps.

<div class="lesson-tag"><span class="lt lab">Hands-on lab</span><span class="lm">15 min</span></div>

## Try one in MATLAB Online {#try-one-in-matlab-online}

You do not need a MATLAB license: [MATLAB Online](https://www.mathworks.com/products/matlab-online.html) runs in a browser with a MathWorks account. The [MATLAB guide](../matlab/guide.qmd) walks through the setup. Then open the first live script directly:

<a href="https://matlab.mathworks.com/open/github/v1?repo=filhoalm/matisse-learn&file=downloads/MATISSE_1_Overview.mlx"><img src="../images/open-in-matlab-online.svg" alt="Open in MATLAB Online" width="136" height="20"></a>

Work through the Overview live script one section at a time. Find the `sift` and `sage` lines on the system map, then use `help sage/sage` in MATLAB to read how SAGE is called.

<div class="lesson-tag"><span class="lt quiz">Self-check</span><span class="lm">3 min</span></div>

## Self-check {#self-check}

::: {.quiz data-answer="2"}
**What does SAGE do?**

1. It compares groups with likelihood-ratio tests.
2. It smooths the observed rates with SIFT and then fits the New APC model to the smoothed rates.
3. It draws the four standard plots.

::: explain
SAGE is a two-step approach: denoise the rates, then fit the New APC model. Its estimable functions are smoother than those of the standard model, which helps most when counts are modest.
:::
:::

::: {.quiz data-answer="1"}
**Which of these tools is in `matisseR` but not in the MATLAB toolbox?**

1. Social generation contrasts and cohort shares.
2. SIFT smoothing.
3. Joinpoint regression.

::: explain
The generation and share tools are additions in `matisseR`. SIFT, SAGE, EPIPHANY and joinpoint are in the MATLAB toolbox only, for now.
:::
:::
